name: Lion's Mane
summary: Tooth fungus. Moderate fresh air, since too much air yellows the spines.
chamber_notes: If spines brown or yellow, cut fresh air and raise humidity slightly. Original Shrooly lion's mane recipe used a gentle fan ramp.

source_notes.title: Stamets
source_notes.detail: Paul Stamets, Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms (commonly cited chamber ranges). H. erinaceus colonizes ~21 to 24 °C and fruits cooler, often 16 to 20 °C.

source_notes.title: Vendor cards
source_notes.detail: Published grow-card ranges from culinary spawn suppliers (FreshCap, North Spore, Out-Grow and similar). Lion's mane cards usually 85 to 95% humidity and 8 to 12 h light.

source_notes.title: Stock firmware
source_notes.detail: Shipped lion's mane LUA: 10 h photoperiod, 5% white LED, ramped fan over ~161 s.

stages.name: Pinning
stages.notes: Look for dense white primordia, not fuzzy overlay.

stages.name: Fruiting
stages.notes: Harvest when spines elongate but before they yellow.

light_recipe.why: Colonization is dark to limit early pins. Fruiting uses 12 h and 26% white, mapped from Jozifek et al. 2025 additional tests at 200 lux on a 12 h cycle, which produced white basidiocarps. Their main 500 lux treatment was 24 h continuous light and caused pink stress coloring, so that schedule is not used. RGB is the general blue mix; that paper used white fluorescent, not a measured blue ratio.
light_recipe.wavelength_note: WS2812 blue is roughly 465 to 475 nm. The RGB mix is an approximation of cited wavelengths, not a measured spectrum.

sources.title: Jozifek et al. 2025
sources.detail: Miroslav Jozifek et al., Selenium Uptake by Hericium erinaceus Basidiocarps, Agriculture 15 (2025). The main cultivation used 500 lux for 24 h continuous light and caused pink stress coloring. Additional tests at 200 lux or lower on a 12 h cycle produced white basidiocarps. This recipe uses that 200 lux, 12 h schedule. 200 lux maps to 26% white.

sources.title: Sakamoto 2018
sources.detail: Yuichi Sakamoto, Influences of environmental factors on fruiting body induction, development and maturation in mushroom-forming fungi, Fungal Biology Reviews 32 (2018). Light is a fruiting cue for many basidiomycetes. Blue light is the usual photomorphogenesis signal. Agaricus bisporus is called out as not needing light for a cap. Flammulina velutipes can fruit in the dark as a long stem with a tiny cap.

sources.title: Stamets
sources.detail: Paul Stamets, Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms, Ten Speed Press. Used here as a general cultivation reference. This recipe does not take a photoperiod or lux number from a cited page in that book.
